clue.text: Girls are mad for this Black Label Dior creation

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: a creation is something newly made up, so the words before it are refashioned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A black-labelled design from the fashion house Dior is the item every girl is wild about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a couture label; in fact Black is just B and the rest is shuffled into BARBIE DOLL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbie doll is the famous toy figure that generations of young girls have been passionate about.

clue.text: Group of girls getting drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flock or company, especially of young women
second meaning: British slang for an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A gang of young women heads off for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a bevvy or bevy is a drink, usually beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is the traditional collective noun for a company of girls or ladies, and also informal for an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Turning paler, son beginning to experience setback

indicators.note: turning means changing form, so the letters of the colour word are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of experience

explanation.surface: A patient going pale while their son starts to feel worse suffers a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into illness after improvement, so a reversal or setback.

clue.text: Cap such activity between countries?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a player chosen to represent their country, who is awarded a cap
second meaning: describing something that takes place across national borders

explanation.walkthrough: Cap looks like a verb meaning limit; in British sport a cap is a player picked for the national team, and such a player is called an international.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who has represented their nation is an international, and the adjective describes dealings between nations.

clue.text: Bug in the house? It's muted after work

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters are reworked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A listening device planted in a house is switched off once the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: Bug suggests a spy's microphone, which fits muted; it is a real insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Dust mites are tiny arachnids living in household dust, a domestic creepy-crawly or bug.

clue.text: Utah's top Republican wearing hat that's glaringly bright

indicators.note: something worn goes around the wearer, so the headgear encloses the other letters

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Utah
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A senior Utah politician sports a hat of dazzling colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid describes colours that are vivid to the point of being garish or glaring.

clue.text: Use computer to break in horse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to gain unauthorised access to a computer system
second meaning: a horse for ordinary riding, or a worn-out one

explanation.walkthrough: Break in a horse means to train it, which leads the eye to a single horsey phrase; the clue splits after break in.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack is to intrude into a computer system illicitly, and a hack is also an old riding horse.

clue.text: Complaint has soldiers punching first-class lieutenant

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the digit 1 read as letter I

indicators.note: a fist punching goes into its target, so the troops sit inside the officer's letters

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
men are soldiers in the ranks

explanation.surface: A grievance arises because troops have assaulted a top-notch junior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Child born Sean, famous actor, bored by Yankee foodstuff

indicators.note: a thing bored by a drill has a hole made in it, so a letter is driven into the middle

parts.note: a kid is a child
né is French for born, used of men's former names
Sean Bean is an English actor
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A birth notice reads like a child named Sean becoming a famous actor in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Né is the masculine of née; the Y slips between it and the actor's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidney beans are a common edible pulse, a staple foodstuff in chilli and stews.

clue.text: Man Tel Aviv sent back, not very independent

indicators.note: something sent back travels the way it came, so the city's letters run the other way
not tells us to leave out the letters for the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written; that its first five letters read backwards spell the answer is a coincidence of the deletion, not a separate hiding
V is the abbreviation for very
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A man is deported from Israel and is left barely self-sufficient.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one V and the I from the city's name leaves TELAV before it is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Man in its old sense of manservant is a gentleman's personal attendant, a valet.

clue.text: Sat across street, looking dishevelled

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
raddled means worn out and unkempt in appearance

explanation.surface: Someone sits across the road, looking a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Sat across looks like sat on the other side of; here it means sat with legs either side.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle something is to sit astride it with one leg on each side, so straddled matches sat across.

clue.text: Lean classic good — not ordinary — chorizo, VAT free

indicators.note: letters set free are no longer held in their original order and can be rearranged
not instructs us to remove the letter for the word that follows it

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
taken as written, a spicy sausage
taken as written, value added tax

explanation.surface: A tasty, lean chorizo with no tax added is praised as a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: Lean is not a description of meat but the film director David Lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Zhivago is David Lean's celebrated 1965 film, one of the director's classics.

clue.text: Fiddle my per diem cash in complex rip-off

indicators.note: to fiddle accounts is to tamper with them, so these letters are tampered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to fiddling their daily expenses as part of an elaborate swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiddle wants to be the definition, a fraud; it is the anagram signal and the definition is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyramid scheme is an elaborate fraud in which early investors are paid with later recruits' money.

clue.text: Driving Macron to Le Casino here?

definitions.text: Driving Macron to Le Casino here?

indicators.note: driving things along jostles them about, so the letters that follow are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone chauffeurs the French president to a famous casino.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the place is famous for its casino and for the Monte Carlo Rally driving event.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte Carlo in Monaco is home to the famous Casino and gives its name to a motor rally.

clue.text: Makes too much drama of past deeds

parts.note: something over is finished, in the past
acts are deeds

explanation.surface: Someone fusses theatrically over things they did long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to perform in an exaggerated, hammy way, making too much drama.

clue.text: In which to soak Trump's bottom? Oh, that's totally laid back!

indicators.note: laid back literally means set down facing backwards, so the letters read from the end

parts.note: butt is American slang for the buttocks, fitting an American president
taken as written

explanation.surface: A relaxing tub would let the president soak his backside, which sounds very chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump's bottom looks like a final letter selection giving P; it is the American word for a rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot tub is a heated outdoor bath where people sit and soak.

clue.text: Swindle can upset European Union? Proceed!

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a tin is a can

indicators.note: something upset in a down clue is turned upside down, so the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: EU is the abbreviation for European Union

explanation.surface: A fraud could unsettle the European Union, yet the speaker urges carrying on.
explanation.definitionFit: Continue is an imperative telling someone to carry on, the same as proceed.

clue.text: Retro picture featuring Circle Line?

indicators.note: the run of words features the solution, carrying it inside them across the gap

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An old-style photograph of the London Underground's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground line; here it means a circle of latitude, and the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are circles of latitude, lines drawn around the globe.

clue.text: Old King catching part of Hamlet's soliloquy in autumn time

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: catching means holding something within, so the monarch's letters go around the quotation

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles
the soliloquy begins with the words to be

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch recites a bit of Hamlet during the autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: October is a month of autumn in the northern hemisphere, so a time of that season.

clue.text: Japanese film icon's health has worsened, it's reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the words counts, not the spelling

parts.note: an icon is a god-like idol
someone whose health has worsened is iller

explanation.surface: A news item says a famous Japanese screen star is in declining health.
explanation.walkthrough: Say god's iller in a non-rhotic British accent and you get the monster's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Godzilla is the giant monster of the 1954 Japanese film and its many sequels.

clue.text: Willowy Kate Moss illustrated back covers

indicators.note: back tells us to read the run of letters from right to left
the words cover the solution, holding it within them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A slender model, Kate Moss, appears on magazine back covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome means lithe and slim, as is a willowy figure.

clue.text: Whip Conservative A-list Etonian into shape

indicators.note: whipping something into shape reforms it, so the letters are reformed into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A party whip is told to bring a celebrity old Etonian Tory into line.
explanation.walkthrough: Whip suggests a party enforcer at Westminster; it is the definition, a lash. An Etonian is a pupil of Eton, an elite English school.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip with nine knotted cords, once used for naval floggings.

clue.text: Conk broken by one bang, perhaps

indicators.note: something broken by an intruder has had it forced into its middle

parts.note: conk is British slang for the nose
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nose is broken by a single blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bang is one example of a loud sound, so of noise, which the word perhaps flags.

clue.text: Corrupt wager placed around noon

indicators.note: placed around means set on all sides, so the gamble surrounds the time of day

parts.note: a bet is a wager
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A dishonest bet is laid at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is British slang for dishonest or crooked, as in a bent copper.

clue.text: Rising actress Wilson a hero

parts.note: Rebel Wilson is an Australian actress
a lion is a brave or celebrated person

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming actress, Wilson, is hailed as a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Rising looks like describing a star actress; it is the noun, an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising or revolt, the same as a rebellion.

clue.text: Regained consciousness requiring pan in A&E

indicators.note: in here places the cooking vessel inside the hospital department's letters

parts.note: A&E is a hospital's accident and emergency department
a wok is a Chinese frying pan

explanation.surface: A patient came round in casualty needing a bedpan.
explanation.definitionFit: To wake is to come out of sleep or unconsciousness, so awoke is the past tense for regaining it.

clue.text: One may eat people, so gets repelled?

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back the way it came, so the letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so

explanation.surface: Someone who eats people would naturally find others are repelled by them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres in folklore are giants who devour humans.

clue.text: Charitable inclination to collect English novel works

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so the leaning word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination or talent
E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: works here is a verb, the book's letters working themselves into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A generous urge prompts someone to gather English novels and works.
explanation.walkthrough: Works looks like a noun in a list with novel; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Benevolent means kindly and generous, the disposition of someone given to charity.
